title: Model persistence and format versioning
goal: Implement a checkable roundtrip and candidate-based loading that preserves the old model on failure.

prerequisites.text: Modules 1–5: functions, STL, ownership, testing and multi-file builds.
Study the linked prerequisite topics below before this lesson.

sections.title: A format is an interface
paragraphs: Saved data may outlive a program version. A format needs an explicit marker and field definitions. Teaching format EV1 stores an element count and values in 0…100. A future EV2 cannot be guessed to mean EV1: identical numbers might have different meanings. Reject unknown versions before mutation, and treat migration as a separate checkable algorithm.

EV1 3 1 2 3 declares three values; EV1 2 1 is incomplete, while EV1 0 extra contains unexpected data. Whitespace between tokens is flexible but extra tokens are forbidden. A count limit of eight bounds memory and the teaching scenarios. If a product needs more data, revise the limit and tests explicitly.

sections.title: Loading with a strong guarantee
paragraphs: load first validates version and count, then constructs a separate candidate vector. It validates every value before appending it and checks end of input after the last item. Only a completely valid record permits model.swap(candidate). Before swap the model still holds its previous data, so rejection requires no manual restoration of overwritten elements.

The initial laboratory model contains 99. Every malformed record prints rejected 99, making preservation observable. An additional test should first load another valid model, then reject malformed data and compare against that updated model. This detects an implementation that simply recreates the original 99 on every failure.

sections.title: Guided model
paragraphs: Implement a checkable roundtrip and candidate-based loading that preserves the old model on failure.
steps: Agreement checks one simple concrete roundtrip.

sections.title: Roundtrip and canonical output
paragraphs: save writes the version, count and values in a fixed order with a final newline. After loading, the program saves to an ostringstream, reloads those bytes into copy and compares vectors. The property load(save(model))==model checks agreement between the operations, but does not replace independently specified expected records.

Both functions can share a mistake, such as consistently omitting the first element. Also check explicit cases EV1 0 and EV1 3 1 2 3 against exact stdout. Writing to a real stream requires checking open, write and close outcomes. Successful in-memory serialization does not establish that a device has physically persisted a file.

sections.title: Nexus filesystem boundaries
paragraphs: Console-run files belong to a per-process virtual filesystem. Creating a file does not automatically create a personal document on a phone. Transfer results through explicit artifact saving into the project and export. The laboratory uses stdin and memory to test the format independently of device access and without hidden writes to a user project.

Graphical TaskFlow permits a specific taskflow.txt file and uses NXTF1 with different fields. Renaming EV1 to NXTF1 does not make the formats compatible. The shared principle is to validate a bounded candidate and commit it as a whole. A portable archive includes sources and selected data, never the owner’s session, cookies or secrets.

sections.title: Compatibility and corruption
paragraphs: Enumerate unknown versions, negative counts, excessive counts, incomplete records, out-of-range values and trailing data. Preserve the previous model for every rejection. Add a valid whitespace variant and compare normalized output. Filenames and user text must not become operating-system commands or unrestricted output paths.

An independent EV0→EV1 migration requires a documented old format and tests for both versions. Do not automatically interpret a missing marker as a legacy version. Separate established results—parsing, roundtrip and model preservation—from untested properties such as power failure, external disks, concurrent writes and synchronization across devices.

sections.title: Boundary and extension
paragraphs: Implement a checkable roundtrip and candidate-based loading that preserves the old model on failure.

sections.title: Laboratory contract: input to observation
paragraphs: The format is EV1 count values, with count=0…8, values=0…100 and whitespace-only trailing input. Failure preserves old model {99} and prints rejected 99. On success save in memory, reload into a copy and compare; stdout is the canonical EV1 record.

Trace the first reference scenario before running. Exact stdin: "EV1 3 1 2 3". Expected stdout: "EV1 3 1 2 3\n" Relate each algorithm step to state changes, distinguishing rejection from the point where a change is committed.

sections.title: Reading a working example
paragraphs: ostringstream produces EV1 and seven. istringstream reads those bytes back. Agreement checks one simple concrete roundtrip. First identify data, ownership and the observable outcome. Then change exactly one initial condition and predict which observation changes. This connects syntax to a contract rather than memorizing finished source text.

The old vector contains nine. Candidate 1,-2 is rejected before swap. false and nine demonstrate preservation. Compare the second example with the first: what new boundary is covered, and which test distinguishes the correct implementation from a superficially similar mistake? Retain both sources, predictions and actual observations so that the explanation can be reproduced.

sections.title: Independent checking and transfer
paragraphs: Propose an EV0→EV1 specification and tests. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Begin with a specification and input bounds; the worked function is a scaffold, not the requirements of another domain. State an independent expectation before execution so that a test is not fitted to accidental output.

Distinguish process memory, a saved project artifact and device export. Retain a checkable result and an independent trace. Explain the selected contract and supply an independent example. Record decisions, a rejected alternative, checked scenarios and remaining limitations. Independently complete the final assessment control-change task and explain which files, tests and observations it affects. An additional peer or teacher requirement is optional review.

selfcheck.prompt: Starting from model{99}, load receives EV1 2 1. What should it do?
selfcheck.feedback: Two values were declared but only one supplied. An incomplete candidate cannot be committed.

selfcheck.prompt: Why is EV1 0 extra rejected while EV1 0 followed by a newline is accepted?
options: Only whitespace is permitted after the values.
An empty model is forbidden with any trailing input.
The word extra counts as a zero value.
selfcheck.feedback: count 0 is valid but does not remove complete-input validation. Whitespace is not an additional record field.

selfcheck.prompt: Which experiment actually checks a model roundtrip?
options: Print the same buffer twice without loading.
Save, load into another model and compare values.
selfcheck.feedback: A roundtrip must exercise both conversions. Identical repeated prints do not test deserialization.

selfcheck.prompt: An unknown EV2 record arrives. May it be treated as EV1 because its numbers look similar?
options: Yes, if the current model is still empty.
No: a version specification and explicit migration path are required.
Yes, if its first value is 0.
selfcheck.feedback: Identical-looking fields may have different meanings in a new version. Similar syntax does not establish semantic compatibility.

selfcheck.prompt: Which negative test detects reset-to 99 instead of a strong guarantee?
options: First load{7} successfully, then reject corrupt input and expect{7}.
Only reject corrupt input starting from{99}.
selfcheck.feedback: The first test separates current and startup state. Starting from{99}, both algorithms could appear correct.

selfcheck.prompt: Explain the swap commit point and preservation of 99.
selfcheck.feedback: Next: Event testing and reproducible traces. Preserve your project and experiment results.

practice.title: Laboratory: Model persistence and format versioning
practice.task: The format is EV1 count values, with count=0…8, values=0…100 and whitespace-only trailing input. Failure preserves old model {99} and prints rejected 99. On success save in memory, reload into a copy and compare; stdout is the canonical EV1 record.
criteria: The full input and output contract is satisfied.
Invariants and lifetimes are explained; rejection preserves the model.
Ordinary, empty, boundary and failure scenarios are covered.
Test rejection following an earlier successful load.
An independent extension and test are supplied, rather than only a reference copy.
Sources, actual observations and limits of conclusions are retained.
practice.hint: Do not compare strings alone: load the saved text into another model and compare values.

steps.action: Preserve your work and create a separate project for experiments.
Open Task and Code Studio and copy the starter and listed files.
Before running, record the expected transitions and outcome of every case.
Execute every reference case and retain actual observations.
Test rejection following an earlier successful load.
Add an independent case and explain its boundary.
Save sources, the protocol and an explanation of limitations.

terms.definition: Converting a model into an explicitly specified data format.
Validated reconstruction of a model from a data format.
A marker selecting how a record is interpreted.
Checking reconstruction after saving a model.
A consistent representation used when saving data.
An explicit transformation between specified data versions.
A condition preserved at the boundaries of permitted model operations.
An agreed observation by which a client distinguishes contract satisfaction from a defect.
